sentences.text: + W.P.(CRL) 2486/2024 & CRL.M.A. 24148/202  JITENDER KUMAR @ JATIN & ORS.
Th  ve  THE STATE NCT OF DELHI AND ANR

Through: Mr. Anand V. Khat  State with SI Sun  Sunil Kumar, PS N  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANISH DAYAL  OR % 14.08.2024 1.

This petition has been filed for quashing of FIR No.176/2019 under Sections 498A/406/377/354/34 IPC registered at PS Nangloi, Delhi on the basis of settlement arrived at between the parties dated 30 th March, 2024, which is on record of this Court.
2.

As per the settlement, total amount of Rs.5 Lacs had been agreed to be given to the respondent No.2/wife, out of which Rs.1 Lac has already been given at the stage of withdrawal of the DV petition, another Rs.1 Lac has been paid at the stage of the filing of the first motion and Rs.2 Lacs has been tendered today vide DD No.855057 drawn on Punjab National Bank handed over to respondent No.2, who is present in Court.
The balance of Rs.1 Lac is to be tendered at the time of the second motion.
3. Both parties undertake to file the second motion of divorce within 10 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 17/08/2024 at 08:19:16 days from today, as per the settlement.
4. Petitioner and respondent No.2 are present in Court and duly identified by the IO.
Respondent No.2 states that she has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.

5. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

Consequently, the FIR No.176/2019 under Sections Jitender Kumar @ Jatin & Ors vs The State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127444158/
1 498A/406/377/354/34 IPC registered at PS Nangloi, Delhi and proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
6. Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
7. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of.
